subtitle: Lesson 31 · An Illustrative Case Study, Not a Real Incident

eyebrow: The gap: process alive, training long done
code:
# training_job.py (simplified)
def train():
    for epoch in range(40):
        run_epoch()
    save_final_checkpoint()
    # training loop returns here --
    # but a non-daemon upload thread
    # launched earlier never exited

# Kubernetes still sees the container
# as Running -- the Job is never
# marked Completed
caption: A non-daemon thread keeps the process alive long after the real work finished.

code:
Job status:        Running  (for 4 extra days)
DCGM GPU_UTIL:      ~1-2%    (for 4 extra days)

No alert on job duration
No alert on idle GPU utilization

-> discovered Thursday, via the weekly cloud bill
caption: Status alone can't tell a healthy long job from a stalled one -- only elapsed time and real GPU utilization can.

steps.label: TrainingJobRunningTooLong
steps.sub: Fires when a Job runs far longer than its expected duration

steps.label: TrainingGPUIdle
steps.sub: Fires when DCGM GPU_UTIL stays under 5% for 30+ minutes on a training node

steps.label: Together
steps.sub: Each catches a failure shape the other one would miss

code:
- alert: TrainingGPUIdle
  expr: avg_over_time(
    DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL{node_role="gpu-training"}[30m]
  ) < 5
  for: 30m
  annotations:
    summary: >
      GPU utilization under 5% for 30+ min --
      job likely stalled or finished without exiting
caption: Would have fired within an hour of the job actually finishing, not four days later.
